children: Indian benchmark indices are likely to see a flat to positive start on October 19, tracking GIFT Nifty, which was trading with a gain of 85 points at around 23,111.50 in early trade.
Track the latest updates on GIFT Nifty right here on Moneycontrol
Indian equity markets extended their rally for the second consecutive session on October 16, supported by buying in IT, media and metal stocks.

Despite weak global cues, the benchmark indices came under selling pressure in the initial hour of trade but gradually recovered as the session progressed. The Nifty climbed to an intraday high of 23,149.85 and ended the session near the day's high, reflecting sustained buying interest.
At close, the Sensex was up 413.66 points or 0.56 percent at 74,729.27, and the Nifty was up 148.80 points or 0.65 percent at 23,146.15.
Both the benchmark extended the gains for the second consecutive week, with BSE Sensex adding 3.1 percent and Nifty50 rising 2.7%.
The broader markets underperformed the benchmark indices, with the Nifty midcap and smallcap indices ended with marginal losses.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Flat)
GIFT Nifty was trading higher at around 23,111.50 in early trade, indicating a flat to positive start for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Markets (Down)
Asian share markets slipped on Monday as unease over AI's enormous funding needs undermined confidence ahead of a week packed with earnings, while the euro eased in the wake of rioting across France.
US Equities (Slip)
Wall Street tumbles as worries about AI trade and high oil prices weigh
Wall Street tumbled on Friday, with CoreWeave, Broadcom and other AI-related ​technology stocks under renewed pressure, while a jump in oil prices spooked traders heading into the weekend.
Dollar Index (Flat)
The Dollar Spot Index was little changed against the other major currencies, in the early Monday trade.
US Bond Yield (Mixed)
Benchmark 10-year Treasury yields down marginally to 5.06%, while yield on the US 2-year Treasury bond up little bit at 4.71%.
Asian Currencies (Mixed)

Asian currencies traded mixed against the US dollar, with the Indonesian rupiah recording the biggest decline, falling 0.49 percent. The Philippine peso and Taiwan dollar also weakened by 0.27 percent each, while the South Korean won slipped 0.13 percent. On the other hand, the Japanese yen strengthened 0.08 percent, followed by the Chinese renminbi, which rose 0.06 percent. The Thai baht and Malaysian ringgit edged higher by 0.06 percent and 0.03 percent, respectively, while the Singapore dollar eased 0.04 percent.
Crude (Down)
Oil prices slipped on Monday after US President Donald Trump waived sanctions and tariffs on Russia that may lead to more Russian fuel exports.
Brent crude futures fell $1.43, or 1.30%, to $108.43 a barrel after settling at its highest since May 19 on Friday.
US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $100.88 a barrel, down 53 cents, or 0.52%.
Gold (Up)
Gold opened the week higher as traders pared bets on the Federal Reserve raising interest rates this month after remarks by Chair Kevin Warsh.

Bullion was trading around $4,180 an ounce, after falling 0.7% the week before. Traders unwound bets on the probability of a quarter-point hike to less than one-in-five after comments by the Fed chair were interpreted as supporting the case to keep rates on hold when it meets next week.
Fund Flow Action

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) turned net buyers on October 16 after remaining net sellers for 15 consecutive sessions, purchasing equities worth around Rs 1,166 crore. Meanwhile, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) snapped their 45-session buying streak, offloading equities worth Rs 3,661 crore during the session.
